title: Incorporate C-Corp
summary: Set up a new Delaware C-Corporation with standard startup structure including bylaws, stock purchase agreements, and initial board resolutions.

parts.title: Choose formation service
parts.guidance: Compare services against the remaining formation work: Delaware incorporation, registered-agent service, bylaws and initial resolutions, founder stock documents, and handling of an 83(b) election where applicable. Check which items the proposed package includes, which require separate purchases, and what recurring charges follow setup. Distinguish document preparation from actual filing, and confirm how completed records will be delivered. Finish with a selected provider and package, plus a clear list of work that someone else must complete.

options.title: Form through Clerky
options.summary: Compare Clerky’s pay-per-use incorporation with its Company Lifetime Package against the paperwork you expect to need after formation. Both include expedited Delaware filing and the first year of registered-agent service; post-incorporation setup is a separate purchase under pay-per-use. Check the current package terms, excluded third-party charges and later registered-agent costs before choosing. Record the selected package and identify who will handle any work outside it, including the actual submission of an 83(b) election where applicable.
options.when: Forming through Clerky rather than Stripe Atlas — pay-per-document pricing

cost.note: Pay-per-use incorporation (includes expedited Delaware filing fees and the first-year registered agent); the $819 Company Lifetime Package adds unlimited standard post-incorporation paperwork products, and post-incorporation setup is $299 separately on pay-per-use.
Stripe Atlas's published one-time fee (includes the Delaware government fees and the first year of registered agent service); other services and attorney-led formation differ.

parts.title: Check name availability
parts.guidance: Have the exact proposed legal name, including its corporate ending, and a few alternatives ready. Obtain an availability result from Delaware’s dedicated name checker or through your formation provider, and record the spelling and date checked. Resolve an unavailable name before preparing the filing. If filing will happen later, decide whether to reserve the name; checking availability alone does not reserve it. Hand off the checked name and any reservation confirmation for use in the Certificate of Incorporation.

verify.how: Retain the result for the exact proposed legal name from Delaware’s dedicated name-availability checker or the formation provider, including the date checked. If a reservation was requested, retain its separate confirmation; an availability check alone does not reserve the name.

failureModes.what: The name is not distinguishable from an existing entity of record, or lacks a required corporate word (association, company, corporation, incorporated, limited...).
failureModes.then: Pick a distinguishable name or obtain the consent § 102(a)(1) allows (rule card us-de.incorporation-certificate-contents); a cleared name can be reserved for 120 days for $75 on the published fee schedule.

parts.title: Submit incorporation filing
parts.guidance: Choose the jurisdiction and legal form before preparing the filing. Those choices determine the formation documents, signatories and registration authority. Confirm that your formation provider supports the selected route and agree who will prepare, approve and submit the application. Use the instructions for that route to assemble the filing; each regional alternative here describes its own registration step, without establishing that the other formation steps apply in that jurisdiction.

options.title: Default — Delaware Division of Corporations
options.summary: Review the draft Certificate of Incorporation against the agreed formation details and Delaware’s required contents: legal name, registered agent and Delaware office, business purpose, authorized shares and par value or no-par designation, incorporator details, and any required class terms or initial-director details. Confirm the intended share authorization; allocating stock to founders happens separately. Approve the final certificate, arrange for the incorporator’s signature and submission through the chosen provider, and confirm the required fee arrangements. Retain submission evidence for follow-up and receipt of the filed certificate.

verify.how: Retain the submission confirmation for follow-up, then confirm acceptance from the returned Certificate of Incorporation bearing Delaware’s Filed endorsement. A general entity-search result is not a certificate of good standing.

cost.note: Minimum state filing fee for a one-page, minimum-stock Certificate of Incorporation — the schedule marks it 'varies based on stock'. Expedited options on the same schedule, per document: $50 24-hour, $100 same-day, $500 2-hour (Priority 2), $1,000 1-hour (Priority 1).

failureModes.what: The Division rejects the filing because the certificate is defective — missing § 102(a) required contents or § 103 execution.
failureModes.then: Fix the defect and resubmit: the corporation exists only once the Secretary of State endorses the instrument 'Filed' (rule card us-de.incorporation-filing-mechanics); nothing is committed until that endorsement.

options.title: India - MCA SPICe+ filing
options.summary: Start from the agreed company type, proposed or approved name, and business-activity classification for SPICe+. Review MCA’s name and trademark alerts, then keep the company details consistent across Part A, Part B and the required linked forms. Use the current MCA instructions to confirm the documents and digital signatures needed for your application. Submit the required signed forms as a complete filing, retain the application reference, and monitor the filing dashboard for queries or resubmission requests. Name reservation alone does not complete incorporation.

references.title: MCA SPICe+ name and company information

options.title: UK - Companies House filing
options.summary: Gather the company name, registered office and email address, director and people-with-significant-control details, business activity code, and documents for the chosen company type. Check the share and shareholder information for a company limited by shares, or the guarantor information for one limited by guarantee. Confirm the applicable identity-verification requirements and personal codes before submitting through Companies House or the selected formation agent. Retain the application confirmation and follow up on acceptance; the resulting certificate records the company number and formation date.

references.title: Companies House - set up a limited company

cost.note: £100 Companies House fee for the online incorporation (£124 by post) — published in GBP only, so no USD figure is claimed; online registrations usually complete within 24 hours.

options.title: Germany - notarized GmbH/UG formation
options.summary: Agree with the notary whether you are forming a GmbH or a UG and whether the formation can use the applicable video procedure. The route includes preparing and notarizing the formation documents, satisfying the capital-contribution requirements, and applying for entry in the Handelsregister. Keep the chosen legal form, shareholder contributions and management details consistent throughout. Completion depends on the register entry, not merely the notarization appointment. Use the following four steps to track that sequence with the notary.

parts.title: Prepare the formation deed with the notary
parts.guidance: Give the notary the proposed company name, German registered office, business purpose, intended share capital, each shareholder’s subscription and the proposed managing directors. Confirm whether the articles need provisions beyond the simplified model procedure and identify any non-cash contributions before drafting. Review the resulting documents against those decisions, including the allocation and nominal value of the shares. Finish with an agreed draft and a clear list of the people or authorized representatives needed for notarization.

parts.title: Notarization appointment (in person or by video)
parts.guidance: Confirm the appointment format with the notary and supply the identity and representation documents the notary requests. Video notarization is available only where its legal and technical requirements are met; arrange an in-person appointment otherwise. Review the final formation documents and resolve differences from the agreed draft before completing the required signatures. Retain the notarized documents and the notary’s instructions for capital payment and registration. The appointment completes notarization; entry in the Handelsregister is still a separate milestone.

references.title: GmbHG section 11: Legal status before registration

parts.title: Pay in the share capital
parts.guidance: Confirm the payment instructions and registration threshold for the chosen legal form with the notary. For a cash-funded GmbH, at least one quarter of each cash share must be paid and the statutory minimum total reached before registration is requested; a UG requires its entire share capital and cannot use contributions in kind. Arrange the required contributions, retain evidence linking each payment to the shareholder and subscription, and provide it for the registration application. Do not apply a GmbH payment threshold to a UG.

references.title: GmbHG section 7: Capital and registration requirements

parts.title: Wait for registration in the Handelsregister
parts.guidance: Confirm with the notary that the registration application and required supporting documents have been submitted, and respond to any questions or corrections raised during review. When the entry is made, obtain the register details and check the company name, registered office, share capital, managing directors and representation arrangements against the approved documents. Retain the register evidence with the formation records. The GmbH or UG exists as such on registration; a submitted application alone does not establish that this step is complete.

references.title: GmbHG section 11: Legal status before registration
GmbHG section 7: Capital and registration requirements
GmbHG section 11: Legal status before registration

cost.note: Notary fees are statutory under GNotKG — value-based (Geschäftswert) via the Kostenverzeichnis (Annex 1 to § 3(2)) — plus Handelsregister fees; the amount scales with share capital, so no single sticker price exists.

options.title: France - INPI guichet unique filing
options.summary: For a SAS or SASU, assemble the signed statutes, capital-deposit evidence, legal-notice publication evidence, and the company-address and management documents required for the chosen structure. Prepare the beneficial-owner information and check the application’s activity and tax selections against the company’s actual circumstances. Use the Guichet unique’s requested-document list to complete the filing, then review, sign and pay for the submission. Retain the receipt and monitor requests for corrections. Submission evidence is a handoff to registration review, not confirmation that registration has finished.

parts.title: Receive Certificate of Incorporation
parts.guidance: Collect the Certificate of Incorporation bearing Delaware’s “Filed” endorsement from your formation provider. Compare the returned document with the version approved for filing, and record the filing date and any later effective date specified in the certificate. Resolve discrepancies before relying on the document. Store the complete filed copy for subsequent company setup. If a bank or another recipient requests a certified copy or evidence of good standing, confirm its requirements before ordering additional documents.

verify.how: The complete Certificate of Incorporation bearing Delaware’s Filed endorsement is retained and matches the approved filing. Check each recipient’s requirements before ordering a certified copy or certificate of good standing.

cost.note: Optional certified copy of the filed certificate: $50 per document plus $2 per page (expedited $60 same-day / $50 24-hour). The plain stamped copy comes back with the filing itself at no extra fee.

failureModes.what: The stamped certificate copy is lost.
failureModes.then: Request a replacement copy from the Division and confirm the recipient’s requirements before ordering certification. The published fee schedule lists a certified copy at $50 per document plus $2 per page.

parts.title: Prepare bylaws & initial resolutions
parts.guidance: Use the filed certificate, the initial director and officer choices, and the formation package supplied by your provider or counsel to prepare the bylaws and initial consents. Review the provisions governing board size, meeting quorum, voting and written consent, and check that officer titles and duties match the proposed appointments. Resolve conflicts with the certificate and any template choices that do not fit the intended setup. Finish with consistent, reviewed drafts and the appropriate signatories identified for the following signing step.

parts.title: Sign the bylaws and initial board consent
parts.guidance: Review the final bylaws and organizational consents together so the company name, directors, officer appointments and referenced documents agree. Confirm who has authority to adopt the bylaws and which people must approve each consent. For a unanimous written board consent, obtain every director’s consent through the permitted signing process. Save the adopted bylaws and completed consents in the company records, with their effective dates. This step is complete when the required approvals are documented, rather than when draft documents have merely been generated.

parts.title: Prepare the founder stock issuance
parts.guidance: Prepare each founder’s stock purchase documents from the agreed share allocation, class, purchase price and vesting terms. Check that the issuance fits the certificate’s share authorization and the relevant board approval; authorized shares alone do not establish anyone’s ownership. Review vesting, repurchase provisions and any intellectual-property assignment against the actual agreement. Confirm the consideration each founder must provide and how the issuance will be recorded. Hand off consistent, reviewed agreements and the required approvals for execution; do not assume the shares have already transferred.

parts.title: Founders sign the stock purchase agreements
parts.guidance: Have each founder review and sign the final stock purchase agreement, and obtain the company’s required execution. Confirm that the agreed payment or other consideration is delivered and that the issuance follows the applicable approval. Give the completed agreements and transaction evidence to the person maintaining the stock ledger so its entries match the actual issuance. Establish the actual stock-transfer date from the completed transaction; the incorporation date or a signature date alone should not be substituted when calculating an 83(b) election deadline.

references.title: Delaware stock ledger and company records

verify.how: The executed stock purchase agreements plus the matching entries in the company's stock ledger — the retained signed SPAs and the ledger ARE the record; no external registry of private stock issuances exists to query.

parts.title: Sign the 83(b) election
parts.guidance: If an 83(b) election has been chosen for an eligible stock transfer, review the completed election against the stock documents before signing. Check the taxpayer’s name, identification number and address, the property and quantity transferred, actual transfer date, tax year, restrictions, fair market value and amount paid. Resolve missing or inconsistent values rather than assuming that a template is correct. The taxpayer signs the final election and retains a copy for the filing step; signing alone does not submit it to the IRS.

parts.title: File 83(b) election with the IRS
parts.guidance: For an eligible stock transfer where an 83(b) election has been chosen, confirm the actual transfer date and the 30-day filing deadline, including the IRS weekend and legal-holiday rule where relevant. Identify whether a service is handling this election or you must arrange submission yourself. Track the filing against that deadline and retain the signed election with evidence of timely submission. Provide the required copies to the company and any different transferee. A signed form or a provider selection alone is not evidence that filing occurred.

references.title: Stripe Atlas filing evidence and tracking

verify.how: Online submissions through the taxpayer's IRS Online Account produce their own confirmation — retain it. For the mail rail, retain the USPS certified-mail receipt and a date-stamped copy of the election — the IRS sends no acknowledgment, so proof of timely mailing within the 30-day window (rule card us-fed.83b-filing-period) IS the record; if the IRS returns a stamped copy, retain it as the strongest evidence.

cost.note: USPS Certified Mail fee (Notice 123, prices effective 2026-07-12), plus First-Class postage ($0.82 stamped 1 oz letter) and optional return receipt ($2.91 electronic / $4.65 mail). The IRS charges nothing for the election itself.

failureModes.what: The 30-day window passes with no postmarked election.
failureModes.then: There is no cure: the deadline is jurisdictional (rule card us-fed.83b-filing-period) and an election generally cannot be made late or revoked without IRS consent (rule card us-fed.83b-revocation) — what remains is a tax-counsel conversation about the consequences, not a self-help fix.

previewBriefs.guidance: For an eligible stock transfer where an 83(b) election has been chosen, confirm the actual transfer date and the 30-day filing deadline, including the IRS weekend and legal-holiday rule. Atlas describes automatic filing for its C-corp founders; confirm that it is handling this election. Track the filing and retain the signed election. Use Atlas’s proof-of-filing document and the official USPS tracking record to check the mailing event against the deadline. Provide a copy to the company for which services were performed and to any different transferee, then retain the copies with the filing record.

For an eligible stock transfer where an 83(b) election has been chosen, confirm the actual transfer date and the 30-day filing deadline, including the IRS weekend and legal-holiday rule. Clerky’s post-incorporation setup supplies a pre-filled election and filing instructions. Review the form against the completed stock transaction and confirm who will submit it; document preparation does not establish that a filing service has been arranged. Track submission against the deadline, provide the required company and transferee copies, and retain the signed election with evidence of timely filing.

parts.title: File the Statement and Designation by Foreign Corporation with the CA SOS
parts.guidance: If the corporation needs to qualify to do business in California, assemble its exact legal name, formation jurisdiction, principal office addresses and California agent-for-service-of-process details. Obtain the current certificate of good standing required from the jurisdiction where it was formed, and check that the names and jurisdiction agree across the documents. Have an authorized corporate officer approve and sign the Statement and Designation, then submit it through California’s filing service with the required fee. Retain the accepted filing and registration details for the company records.

references.title: CA SOS foreign qualification (filed via bizfile Online)

cost.note: Statement and Designation by Foreign Corporation (stock corporation) filing fee; filed through bizfile Online. Conditional step — excluded from the default-flow fee headline by construction.

parts.title: Appoint a registered agent in each state where you operate
parts.guidance: First identify the states in which the corporation must register or qualify; having customers in a state does not by itself settle that question. For each applicable state, check its agent-for-service-of-process requirements and confirm that the chosen agent can receive official notices there. Agree how notices reach the company and who monitors them, then use the agent’s correct details in the relevant state filing. Keep a state-by-state record of appointments, contact details and renewal arrangements so notices are not lost when people or providers change.

references.title: SBA state registration and registered agents

metadata.supportReason: Clerky/Stripe Atlas have limited APIs. System guides through the process, pre-fills known data, tracks progress, but cannot automate the filing itself.

geoNotes.summary: Incorporate through MCA's SPICe+ integrated form — a single filing covers name reservation, incorporation, PAN, TAN, EPFO/ESIC and optional GST; the government's National Single Window System fronts the process.

Register a private limited company with Companies House — online filings are usually approved within 24 hours, and Companies House exposes a live REST filing API, so software-driven incorporation genuinely exists here.
geoNotes.actionLabel: Companies House — set up a limited company

geoNotes.summary: Form a GmbH (or UG) with a notarized deed — since 2022 the notarial formation can happen by video — and the company exists on registration in the Handelsregister; expect days to weeks, not hours.
Form a SAS/SASU through the INPI guichet unique — the single online portal for all French business formalities since 2023; registration lands in the RCS via INSEE.

Incorporate a Lda or SA through Empresa Online — the registry's own online channel — and the NIPC (which doubles as the company's tax number) arrives with the registration; the in-person Empresa na Hora desks do it same-day.

Incorporate federally under the CBCA through Corporations Canada's online filing (often same-day) — but 25% of directors must be resident Canadians, so non-resident founders often incorporate provincially instead (British Columbia has no residency rule).
